questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word : **PROPHECY**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Prediction**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Prophecy"** refers to a statement or prediction about future events, often made under divine inspiration or considered to be of spiritual significance. (भविष्यवाणी)
 
 
• **Example:** The prophecy foretold a great leader who would unite the kingdom.
 
 
• **"Prediction"** means a forecast or statement about what will happen in the future, often based on evidence or reasoning. (पूर्वानुमान)
 
 
• **Example:** The weather prediction for tomorrow suggests heavy rainfall.
 
 
• Hence, the synonym of **"Prophecy"** is **"Prediction"**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Prediction**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Creation** (सृजन): The act of bringing something into existence.
 
 
• **Example:** The creation of the new artwork took months of meticulous effort.
 
 
 
• **Denial** (अस्वीकार): Refusal to accept or acknowledge something.
 
 
• **Example:** His denial of the accusations surprised everyone.
 
 
 
• **Decision** (निर्णय): A conclusion or resolution reached after consideration.
 
 
• **Example:** The decision to move abroad was not an easy one.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.**

The historian said, "Even if the war had ended earlier, the long-term economic effects would have been equally devastating for the country."

options.text: The historian said that even if the war would have ended earlier, the long-term economic effects would have been equally devastating for the country.
The historian said that even if the war had ended earlier, the long-term economic effects would have been equally devastating for the country.
The historian said that even if the war ended earlier, the long-term economic effects would have been equally devastating for the country.
The historian said that even if the war had ended earlier, the long-term economic effects will have been equally devastating for the country.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The historian said that even if the war had ended earlier, the long-term economic effects would have been equally devastating for the country.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"Even if the war had ended earlier" remains unchanged:**
 
 
• The past perfect tense "had ended" is retained as it is correct in both direct and indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **"would have been equally devastating" remains unchanged:**
 
 
• Modal auxiliary verb "would" and perfect infinitive "have been" are retained to reflect the hypothetical nature of the statement.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• "said" remains unchanged as it is used to report the statement.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Quotation marks from direct speech are removed in indirect speech.
 
• The sentence begins with the reporting clause and is followed by the reported statement.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *The historian said that even if the war had ended earlier, the long-term economic effects would have been equally devastating for the country.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "The historian said that even if the war would have ended earlier, the long-term economic effects would have been equally devastating for the country." 
 
 
• Incorrect: "would have ended" is grammatically incorrect; "had ended" is the correct form in this context.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "The historian said that even if the war ended earlier, the long-term economic effects would have been equally devastating for the country." 
 
 
• Incorrect: "ended" (simple past tense) is inappropriate here; the correct form is "had ended" (past perfect tense).
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "The historian said that even if the war had ended earlier, the long-term economic effects will have been equally devastating for the country." 
 
 
• Incorrect: "will have been" is incorrect in this hypothetical context; the correct form is "would have been."
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.**

He said to her, "I must tell you that I was not the one who broke the vase, as I was not even in the room when it happened."

options.text: He told her that he had to tell her that he had not been the one who had broken the vase, as he was not even in the room when it had happened.
He told her that he had to tell her that he was not the one who had broken the vase, as he was not even in the room when it had happened.
He told her that he must tell her that he was not the one who broke the vase, as he was not even in the room when it happened.
He told her that he had to tell her that he was not the one who had broken the vase, as he had not even been in the room when it happened.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He told her that he had to tell her that he was not the one who had broken the vase, as he was not even in the room when it had happened.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"must" becomes "had to"**
 
 
• In indirect speech, modal verbs like "must" often change to "had to" to reflect the past tense.
 
 
 
• **"was not the one who broke" becomes "was not the one who had broken"**
 
 
• Past simple tense "broke" is converted to past perfect tense "had broken" in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **"was not even in the room when it happened" becomes "was not even in the room when it had happened"**
 
 
• Past simple tense "happened" is converted to past perfect tense "had happened" to match the timeline in indirect speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• The direct quotation is removed, and the sentence is restructured in a narrative form.
 
• Conjunctions like "that" are added to connect the clauses in indirect speech.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *He told her that he had to tell her that he was not the one who had broken the vase, as he was not even in the room when it had happened.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** He told her that he had to tell her that he had not been the one who had broken the vase, as he was not even in the room when it had happened.
 
 
• The phrase "he had not been the one" incorrectly emphasizes the timeline, making the sentence unclear.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** He told her that he must tell her that he was not the one who broke the vase, as he was not even in the room when it happened.
 
 
• The modal "must" is not correctly converted to "had to," which is required in indirect speech.
 
• The past simple tense "broke" and "happened" are not converted to the past perfect tense, making the sentence grammatically incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** He told her that he had to tell her that he was not the one who had broken the vase, as he had not even been in the room when it happened.
 
 
• The addition of "he had not even been" unnecessarily complicates the sentence and alters the meaning slightly.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.**

The tourist, after a long journey, exclaimed with relief that she had finally arrived at her destination.

options.text: The tourist said, "I have finally arrived at my destination!"
The tourist exclaimed with relief, "I finally arrived at my destination!"
The tourist exclaimed with relief, "She finally arrived at my destination!"
The tourist said with relief, "She arrived at her destination!"

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The tourist, after a long journey, exclaimed with relief that she had finally arrived at her destination.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"she had finally arrived" becomes "I have finally arrived"**
 
 
• Pronoun "she" is changed to "I" to match the direct speech format.
 
• Verb "had arrived" is converted to "have arrived" to align with the present perfect tense in direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Indirect: "exclaimed with relief"
 
• Converted to: "exclaimed with relief," maintaining the emotional tone.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "I" and ends with an exclamation mark "!".
 
• Reporting clause follows the quoted speech, separated by a comma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"**The tourist exclaimed with relief, "I finally arrived at my destination!*"*.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The tone of the sentence does not align with the emotional "exclaimed with relief" in the original sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "The tourist exclaimed with relief, "She finally arrived at my destination!""

• **Option 4:** "The tourist said with relief, "She arrived at her destination!""

questions.question:
**Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:**

Why did they have to postpone the crucial board meeting until further notice?

options.text: Why the crucial board meeting had to be postponed until further notice by them?
Why the crucial board meeting was postponed until further notice?
Why had the crucial board meeting to be postponed until further notice by them?
Why did the crucial board meeting have to be postponed until further notice?

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Why did they have to postpone the crucial board meeting until further notice?"
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the crucial board meeting" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "did have to postpone" to "did have to be postponed."
 
• Ensure the question structure is retained with "why" at the beginning.

questions.question:
**Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:**

We saw the new CEO enter the conference room just as the meeting was about to begin.

options.text: The new CEO was seen entering the conference room just as the meeting was about to begin by us.
The new CEO was seen to enter the conference room just as the meeting was about to begin by us.
The new CEO was seen enter the conference room just as the meeting was about to begin by us.
The new CEO had been seen to enter the conference room just as the meeting was about to begin.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "We saw the new CEO enter the conference room just as the meeting was about to begin."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the new CEO" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "saw enter" to "was seen to enter" (past simple passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "us."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"The new CEO was seen to enter the conference room just as the meeting was about to begin by us."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "The new CEO was seen entering the conference room just as the meeting was about to begin by us." – Incorrect, as "entering" changes the meaning.
 
• **Option 3:** "The new CEO was seen enter the conference room just as the meeting was about to begin by us." – Incorrect, as "enter" is not grammatically correct in passive voice.
 
• **Option 4:** "The new CEO had been seen to enter the conference room just as the meeting was about to begin." – Incorrect, as "had been" changes the tense unnecessarily.

questions.question:
In the sentence

"These examinations, which demand years of rigorous preparation, are intended to select only the most capable candidates." what is the part of speech of the word "rigorous"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***A) "Rigorous" qualifies the noun "preparation" in the sentence.***

 
 
• This **means** that "rigorous" is used as an adjective, as adjectives describe or modify nouns.
 
 
 
• ***B) Adjectives provide more information about the noun.***
 
 
• "Rigorous" here describes the type of preparation required for the examinations, emphasizing its intensity and thoroughness.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 3**: Incorrect because a noun is a person, place, thing, or idea, and "rigorous" is describing a noun, not acting as one.
 
• **Option 4**: Incorrect because an adverb modifies a verb, adjective, or other adverb, and "rigorous" is specifically modifying a noun (preparation).

questions.question:
Identify the voice (active or passive) and tense of the verb phrase "are intended" in the sentence:

"These examinations, which demand years of rigorous preparation, are intended to select only the most capable candidates."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3** i.e '**Passive voice, simple present**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb phrase **"are intended"** is in the passive voice, which means the subject is receiving the action of the verb.
 
• **In the simple present tense,** the passive voice is formed by using the present tense of the verb "to be" (am, is, are) followed by the past participle of the main verb.
 
• In this case, "are" is the present tense of the verb "to be", and "intended" is the past participle of the main verb "intend".

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Option 3.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Active voice:** In an active voice sentence, the subject performs the action expressed by the verb. "These examinations select..." is an example of the active voice. 
 
• **Present perfect:** The present perfect tense is formed with "have/has" + the past participle of the verb. For example, "have intended" or "has intended".
 
• **Past perfect:** The past perfect tense is formed with "had" + the past participle of the verb. For example, "had intended".
